  "reasons": [
    "Idea A has a defined payer and sourced pricing: sellers pay at close (6-8% at Acquire.com, 5-10% at Flippa, 5% at MicroExits), with links to published pricing pages. Idea B has no priced direct competitor; its only anchor is an adjacent co-founder-matching service (CoFoundersLab, $29/mo).",
    "Idea A's competitors show that people already pay for this category. Idea B's named competitors are free or pre-launch, and two show dummy or illustrative data. That suggests the category has not yet proven anyone will pay.",
    "Idea B's concept is unresolved. Its own source says 'one-line description to confirm', and the customer is listed as 'varies by idea'. That is a weak base for reaching a paying customer within 90 days.",
    "Idea B's core need is directly contradicted in the same thread offered as demand evidence ('you can just vibe code if you have an idea'). Idea A's demand quotes show real seller pain ('I didn't know where serious buyers were') and real listing supply.",
    "Idea A's case-for gives a concrete wedge suited to a solo operator with AI agents: automating the human-service layer that justifies incumbent fees, aimed at sub-$10k deals. Idea B's wedge ('friend trust network') is unsourced as a differentiator."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea B's demand evidence rests on a single Reddit post, viewed through a mirror site, from someone looking for a collaborator. The same thread contains a direct rebuttal of the premise. The only acquisition-cost figure ($100-200 per paying customer) comes from a vendor blog the brief itself marks as not independently verified.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate. A wins mainly because B is thin and undefined, not because A is strong. A has serious documented risks: five live competitors, three of them at 0% or near-0% commission; a $750 paid placement to a similar audience that produced zero sales; and a comparable marketplace with weak buyer conversion. Because the payer model is a fee at close, getting a paying customer within 90 days depends on a deal actually closing, which is uncertain. Charging a listing fee, or one of the narrower wedges in A's open questions, may be needed to hit the 90-day target."
}
